risk_if_not_implemented: Without Third-Party Libraries, supplier and External Service Provider (ESP) weaknesses, incidents or failures may propagate into the organization's environment unmanaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure (R-SC-1), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Component Impact (R-SC-7), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products (MT-20).

compensating_control_1.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to:
(1) Evaluate security risks and threats associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) supply chains; and
(2) Take appropriate remediation actions to minimize the organization's exposure to those risks and threats, as necessary.
compensating_control_1.justification: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) (TPM-04) provides risk identification and prioritization that compensates for the absence of Third-Party Libraries (CFG-17.1) by enabling informed decisions about where to focus resources to manage residual exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Vulnerability Scanning
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to detect vulnerabilities and configuration errors by routine vulnerability scanning of systems and applications.
compensating_control_2.justification: Vulnerability Scanning (VPM-12) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Third-Party Libraries (CFG-17.1) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses and prioritizing critical remediations. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
